A3.4 Alternative Databases & Data Warehouses HL

HL Unit 5 | Database models, warehouses, OLAP, mining, and distributed systems

Retrieval Practice

Recall A3.3 before comparing database approaches.

  1. What does ACID stand for?
  2. What is the difference between a virtual view and a materialized view?
  3. What does TCL stand for?

Press Down for answers

Answer 1

What does ACID stand for?

Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

Answer 2

What is the difference between a virtual view and a materialized view?

A virtual view stores the query definition. A materialized view stores a snapshot of the result.

Answer 3

What does TCL stand for?

TCL = Transaction Control Language. It manages transactions with commands such as BEGIN TRANSACTION, COMMIT, and ROLLBACK.

HL A3.4.1 database models

Which alternative approaches to storing data are on the spec?

NoSQL = Not Only SQL: flexible data models used in systems such as social media platforms and e-commerce.

Cloud databases: managed services used in software-as-a-service platforms and web systems.

Spatial databases: store and query geographic data for geographic information systems.

In-memory databases: keep data in RAM for real-time analytics and very fast access.

Real-world scenarios: e-commerce platforms, geographic information systems, managed cloud services, real-time analytics, social media platforms, software-as-a-service products.

HL A3.4.2 data warehouse objectives

What makes a data warehouse different from an operational database?

Append-only data: new records are added rather than constantly overwritten.

Subject-oriented data: organized around themes such as sales or customers.

Integrated data: combines data from multiple sources.

Time-variant data: keeps historical data over time.

Non-volatile data: stable for analysis rather than frequent editing.

Optimized for query performance: designed for efficient analysis and reporting.

HL A3.4.3 OLAP and data mining

What do these terms stand for, and what do they do?

OLAP = Online Analytical Processing

OLAP supports analytical queries across large data sets to compare dimensions such as time, region, or product.

Data mining extracts useful patterns and relationships from large data sets.

Uses: trend analysis, customer behavior, fraud patterns, demand forecasting, anomaly spotting.

HL Data mining techniques on the spec

Which techniques must you recognize and describe?

Classification: place data into known categories.

Clustering: group similar data without predefined labels.

Regression: predict a numerical value.

Association rule discovery: find items or events that often occur together.

Sequential pattern discovery: find patterns in ordered events over time.

Anomaly detection: identify unusual or unexpected cases.

HL A3.4.4 distributed databases

What features must a distributed database manage?

Data consistency across different locations.

Concurrency control, data partitioning, replication, and scalability.

Fault tolerance, data security, and global query processing.

Distribution transparency and location transparency mean the system behaves like one database to the user.

ACID still matters because transactions must remain reliable across the distributed system.

🧠 Quick Check HL

A company wants to keep years of sales history from many systems and run trend dashboards without slowing the live checkout system.

Explain why a data warehouse is a better fit than the live transactional database.

A data warehouse keeps integrated, historical, query-optimized data for analysis, while the live system is mainly for day-to-day transactions.

Key Takeaways HL

  • A3.4.1 covers NoSQL, cloud, spatial, and in-memory databases with real-world uses.
  • A3.4.2 covers the objectives and characteristics of data warehouses.
  • OLAP = Online Analytical Processing; data mining includes classification, clustering, regression, association rules, sequential patterns, and anomaly detection.
  • Distributed databases must manage consistency, ACID reliability, transparency, partitioning, replication, security, fault tolerance, and scalability.
